Feature ablation across 4 screening cohorts demonstrates that near-perfect accuracy (AUROC ~ 1.0) is driven entirely by label-leaking questionnaire items, with performance collapsing to chance on demographics alone (AUROC 0.447-0.580).

Leaderboard comparison on full ABIDE I (N=854, 20 sites) showing the scanner generalization gap between site-leaking random cross-validation and honest Leave-One-Site-Out (LOSO) evaluation across 7 model families.

Functional connectomes carry high physical scanner fingerprints (64.87% multi-class site decodability vs 19.91% majority-site chance), while demographic and motion confounds exhibit modest direct diagnostic correlation (LOSO AUROC = 0.5588).

Comparison of fMRI harmonization strategies (None, Site Regression, In-Fold ComBat, and Leaky ComBat) under LOSO, showing no statistically detectable inflation from leaky ComBat at N=854 (Delta = +0.0156, 95% CI [-0.0013, 0.0328], Holm p = 0.2840).
Reliability calibration curves before and after temperature scaling for the adult demographics screener (ECE: 0.0307 -> 0.0278) and ABIDE I LOSO (ECE: 0.2142 -> 0.0408).

one_sentence_caption: Per-site empirical conformal coverage under Leave-One-Site-Out at nominal 90% (alpha=0.10) across all 20 clinical sites, highlighting conservative over-coverage (4 sites) and severe under-coverage (11 sites) due to scanner domain shift.

paper_section: Section V (Selective Prediction & Clinical Triage Policy)
one_sentence_caption: Selective prediction risk-coverage trade-off curves and 3-way triage policy referral rates across leak-free tabular and ABIDE LOSO settings, demonstrating that clinical abstention reduces error without eliminating residual risk.

Empirical audit of 33 published autism ML studies (2013-2026), revealing near-universal behavioral feature leakage in questionnaire models (93.8%), widespread random cross-validation on multi-site data (77.4%), and pervasive neglect of uncertainty quantification (93.9% reporting neither).
